title: At BATS, eight fixed-density-profile sampling tests leave at least 92% of the 1989-2025 AOU rise
abstract: We tested whether shared bottle interpolation can explain the relation between oxygen use and density-layer thickness at BATS. We held eight fitted AOU-density profiles fixed and sampled them at the observed 1989-2025 bottle locations. The false 2016-2025 minus 1989-1998 AOU gain was 0.20-0.90 umol/kg, compared with 11.86 observed. After subtraction, 10.96-11.67 remained. The held-out thickness prediction also remained useful. True bracketing gave null correlations as strong as -0.79, but with small amplitude. Thus correlation alone can be misleading, while this sampling error cannot explain most of the measured gain under the tested profiles. Limits include uncertain reference curvature, one site, sparse bottles and no test of density or oxygen calibration errors. This result does not identify a ventilation or respiration cause.
